name: Derrell Hines Jr.
strengths: Hines beats press with a sudden inside swipe and head fake — crosses the corner's face and creates 2+ yards at the stem.
Hines tracks underthrown deep balls, throttles down, and high-points without breaking stride.
Hines turns bubble screens into YAC — drop-steps downhill and finishes through arm tackles.
weaknesses: Hines still loses some contested fades when DBs get hands in early — needs more functional mass at 6-1 / 170 to shield at the catch point.
comparison: Hines comps to John Metchie III — 6-0/6-1 sudden separator with clean stems, soft tracking hands, and YAC twitch before the frame fully fills out.
projection: Hines projects as a Year 1–2 slot/Z contributor (packages early). Ceiling: every-down SEC WR — the sudden separator with ball skills who grows into contested wins.
schemeFit: Hines fits a Marcus Davis room that wants sudden stems, vertical adjustment, and YAC from the slot or Z.
staffNotes: Vault film desk verified 2026-08-10 from On3 Hudl sophomore embed. Comp size-matched within ~1–2" — not a Florida-alum default.
recruitingStory: Derrell Hines Jr. is a 4-star WR · listed 6-1 / 170 · Carrollwood Day (Tampa, FL) — grew up in Gainesville; summer Swamp visit; Florida among top contenders with return game planned.
angle: Carrollwood WR: press release + tracking + YAC; Gainesville roots + Florida process.
insiderNotes: Hines is a sudden separator who wins at the stem, tracks deep balls clean, and creates YAC. Contested-catch mass is the next growth step. Florida is a top contender with hometown Swamp ties.
